body:
Parent: #13659 under #13216. Implement one bounded numerical foundation before any encoded-image color integration.

Scope and policy, declared before implementation:

- Compose the existing qualified curve evaluators and signed matrix evaluator over owned `matrix_model.ForwardData`.
- Accept explicit finite device RGB binary64 values in [0,1] and an explicit `Relative` request.
- Return the actual linear RGB trace and unclipped relative D50 XYZ binary64 values.
- Recheck public matrix shape, input values, curve domains, and caller sample limits on every call.
- Preserve the existing curve domains, default 4,096-sample limit, and 65,536-sample hard cap.
- Keep the header intent preference independent from the explicit request.

Destination coordinates use binary64 relative D50 XYZ.
The supplied columns already describe PCS coordinates, so this operation applies no additional chromatic adaptation.
It applies no black-point compensation, alpha operation, filtering, output clipping, or integer quantization.
Optional text and adaptation metadata remain unparsed.
A returned `ForwardData` value is numerical input, not a certificate of complete profile conformance or transform eligibility.
The strict JFIF/RGB APIs continue to reject ICC and Exif metadata.

Primary finite criteria, declared before implementation:

1. Each actual linear channel must differ from independent 90-digit Decimal/Fraction curve mathematics by at most 1e-12.
2. Each XYZ channel must lie within two binary64 representable steps of the correctly rounded exact Fraction dot of the actual linear trace.
3. Exact identity/projection bits, negative-zero identities, and declared exact dyadic controls must agree exactly.
4. Full ideal XYZ must satisfy the propagated criterion below, in addition to the component criteria.

For one matrix row, let A be its exact Fraction dot with the actual reported linear values.
Let s be the correctly rounded binary64 value of A.
Let B(A) be the larger exact distance from A to the values two representable steps above and below s.
The allowed absolute difference from the independent ideal XYZ is `row_L1 * 1e-12 + B(A)`.
Here `row_L1` is the sum of the absolute raw row numerators divided by 65,536.
This criterion accounts for rounding across exponent boundaries without changing the existing component tolerances.

Secondary finite offline CMM criterion, declared before implementation:

- Compare the frozen 588-byte profile with SHA256 `3bccbfedf06978c3035b255167afcf462a50b27805096cee038ff4dd69c650a6` through Pillow 12.3.0 / LittleCMS 2.19.
- Use public RGB_DBL to XYZ_DBL APIs, the CMM XYZ profile, relative intent 1, and flags 324.
- Those flags disable optimization, caching, and white fixup. Black-point compensation remains disabled.
- Require absolute XYZ differences of at most 1e-6 on the declared finite frozen-profile sample set.
- Use every RGB triple from `[0,1/255,1/16,1/4,1/2,3/4,15/16,254/255,1]`, plus all 256 neutral byte values.
- Include representable neighbors of the frozen profile branch point, and 256 normalized RGB triples from Python Random seed 13659.

The secondary criterion reflects the reference CMM float32 stages and does not replace the stricter primary mathematics.
It applies only to this frozen profile and declared samples, without a universal precision or compatibility claim.
Synthetic models still receive complete primary checks, with CMM applicability explicit rather than a Fern test skip.
No CMM, Pillow, or C dependency enters the application runtime.

Acceptance:

- [ ] Implement explicit numeric admission, error propagation, owned results, COW isolation, and cooperative cancellation without function values in cells.
- [ ] Check all admitted curve forms, endpoints, branch neighbors, nonfinite inputs, public-value mutations, and invalid or unsupported domains.
- [ ] Check independent math and applicable pinned CMM observations against the criteria above, retaining every discrepancy without tolerance changes.
- [ ] Add a strict file worker, a reproducible reference bundle, and eight meaningful collector fault groups.
- [ ] Commit source before final immutable native/Wasm/ARM campaigns, with nonzero balanced zero-live worker heaps and all selected source/tool hashes unchanged.
- [ ] Pass appropriate full image regressions, Go check/interpreter controls, unchanged complexity gates, and format/build/vet/lint checks.
- [ ] Complete one READY PR through a normal exact-head merge, with truthful CI status, before dependent destination or encoded integration.

Primary reference: ICC.1:2022 sections 8.3.3, 8.4.3, current Table 68, Annex E.4, and normative Annex F.3.
The publisher web reader supplied the document. No local PDF digest is claimed.
These finite numerical policies do not establish general ICC conformance, photographs, physical/process bounds, performance, security, or production acceptance.
All actual M5/epic gates remain open.
